\caption{\textbf{Surrogate-free samplers inside the latent cloud versus uniform sampling on the shell.} The samplers are convex combinations of $k$ encoded ZINC latents (Dirichlet(1) weights) and a Gaussian fitted to them. $\overline{\|z\|}$ is the mean candidate norm. For $k\ge2$ it is estimated by Monte Carlo with $\|z\|^2$ as a control variate, a fixed seed and 2{,}000{,}000--40{,}000{,}000 draws per sampler. The standard error is at most $4.9\times10^{-5}$, and a digit is printed only if it is established. For $k=1$ it is the exact mean norm of the 3,000 cached latents, and the Gaussian fit is exact up to quadrature error. The matched set has $n=440$ completed cells (as in Table~\ref{tab:main}). Means are mean of per-task means; bold marks the highest. $\Delta$ = row minus reference on the same cells. $p_{\mathrm{BH}}$ is corrected over the 8 rows. Tasks = tasks on which the row has the higher mean.}
